newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger amid U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger amid U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger in moderate trade on Tuesday, disregarding weakness in the currency to take direction from gains in U.S. treasuries, dealers said.
"It's the U.S. market's continued follow-through from yesterday's buying when a Fed governor was yapping about no need for a rate hike," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.34 to C$119.17 to yield 6.531 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.62 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to nine basis points from seven basis points at Monday's close.
Canadian and U.S. bonds closed stronger on Monday after U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips hinted there was no immediate need for a U.S. rate hike.

Analysts said today's weakness in the Canadian dollar was not having a significant impact on bond prices. The currency opened weaker at C$1.3951 (US$0.7167). Currency traders said markets were driving the dollar weaker to test the Bank of Canada's resolve to hold interest rates steady.
"The twos (two-year bonds) are technical right now. A lot of people are short twos and even though the currency is weakening, the twos are performing well," the dealer said.

Canadian fixed-income traders were now looking ahead to several key economic releases out later this week, analysts said. They include the U.S. retail sales report for July out on Wednesday and the consumer price index for July on Thursday.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.15 to C$109.03 to yield 6.015 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.33 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 32 basis points from 33 basis points at Monday's close.
